te zullen wegbergen
weg te zullen bergen

glosses: opbergen, verstoppen, verbergen

examples.text: Gedesillusioneerd rolde ik mijn vislijn weer op en borg het haakje weer veilig weg.

glosses: To imprison or incarcerate (someone).

examples.text: In 1970, a new era of "getting tough" on young offenders really began to gather momentum with the incoming Conservative government. The number of juveniles locked up each year increased by 500% between 1965 and 1980.

glosses: To put (something) away in a locked location for safekeeping; (occasionally, chiefly humorously) to sequester (a person) in a similar way.

examples.text: Please lock up all valuables in the safe before leaving.
Angus is back in town! Better lock up your daughters, your wife, and your sheep!

glosses: To close (and often lock) all doors and windows (of a place) securely.
To lock (a door, window, etc.).

examples.text: That door still needs to be locked up.

glosses: To cease responding.

examples.text: When I press this button, the program locks up.

glosses: To cause (a program) to cease responding or to freeze.

examples.text: If your password contains a particular string of letters, entering it can lock up the login form.

glosses: To stop moving; to seize.
To stop moving; to seize.
To stop spinning due to excessive braking torque.

examples.text: Due to the engines-out condition, the landing was conducted without the brake antiskid and normal breaking^([sic]) systems. Because the emergency brake accumulator only provides for a limited amount of brake applications, full braking was applied and retained at the second touch down, resulting in the main wheels locking up. The tires quickly abraded and deflated at a point between about 300 and 450 feet beyond the second and final touch down.

glosses: To lose one's forward momentum; to freeze.
To (mistakenly) cause or have one of one's wheels to lock up (stop spinning).

examples.text: Twelve laps later, Leclerc locked up at the first chicane and clattered over the run-off area. Again, Hamilton got a run on him, and this time Leclerc defended robustly through the flat-out Curva Grande, moving very late to block Hamilton to the Ferrari's left.

glosses: To invest in something long term.
To travel through a flight of locks on a waterway in an uphill direction.
To fasten quoins securely with a mallet and a shooting-stick.
To assure success in or control of (something).

examples.text: He locked up the championship with that move.

glosses: To put (something) in its usual storage place; to place out of the way, clean up.

examples.text: Please put away the tools when you are finished.
I put the clothes away so as to neaten the room.

They burned the old gun that used to stand in the dark corner up in the garret, close to the stuffed fox that always grinned so fiercely. Perhaps the reason why he seemed in such a ghastly rage was that he did not come by his death fairly. Otherwise his pelt would not have been so perfect. And why else was he put away up there out of sight?—and so magnificent a brush as he had too.

glosses: To store, add to one's stores for later use.

examples.text: putting a little away for a rainy day
Preparing for the worst, they put away food for the winter.

glosses: To consume (food or drink), especially in large quantities.

examples.text: You wouldn't think such a small person could put away so much food.
The blonde one, old Bernice, was drinking bourbon and water. She was really putting it away, too.

glosses: To send (someone) to prison or mental asylum.

examples.text: After he was convicted, they put him away for 10 years.

glosses: To kill someone.

examples.text:
It's Decoration Day.
And I knew the Hill Boys would put us away,
but my Daddy wasn't afraid.
He said "We'll fight till the last Lawson's last living day"

glosses: To knock out an opponent.

examples.text: He put away his opponent in the first round.

glosses: To discard, divest oneself of.

examples.text: When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.

glosses: To fend off, deflect; to dismiss.

examples.text: Also he told kynge Arthur that he shold mysse hym / yet had ye leuer than al your landes to haue me ageyne / A sayd the kynge / syn ye knowe of your aduenture puruey for hit / and put awey by your craftes that mysauenture / Nay said Merlyn it wylle not be / soo he departed from the kynge.

glosses: To divorce.

examples.text: And the pharyses cam and axed hym a question: whether it were laufull for a man to putt awaye hys wyfe.

glosses: To take a large lead in a game, especially enough to guarantee victory or make the game no longer competitive.

examples.text: They put the game away by scoring three touchdowns in the fourth quarter.

glosses: To strike out a batter.
To catch a fly ball or tag out a baserunner.
(pickleball) To hit the ball in such a way that the opponent cannot reach it; see passing shot
To close (a building) so that no one can enter.
To terminate (a business).
To put (someone or something) in a secure enclosed space, such as a room or container.

examples.text: The wicked prince was shut up in the castle dungeon.
The engineer had shut the locomotive up in the shed for twenty years.

"You know the doctor's ways, sir," replied Poole, "and how he shuts himself up. Well, he's shut up again in the cabinet; and I don't like it, sir—I wish I may die if I like it. Mr. Utterson, sir, I'm afraid."
"Oh no, snow!" whined Falcon Housebird to her mistress, Queeny Diamond-Heart. I'll be shut up at your house! At your mercy! With no way to get away!"

glosses: Of a person, to stop talking (said by someone, often one in authority, after one has said something annoying, irrelevant, or false, during a period of peace and quiet, or when one is not allowed to talk) or arguing, or (of a person or thing) making noise.

examples.text: You are talking so loud that I can't hear the music – would you mind shutting up?
He was blathering on about something, but I managed to shut him up.
She told us earlier that none of what you just said was true, so shut up!

This is a quote from the letter: "Went to the Senate yesterday and you should have seen the carrying on they did. I could hardly get them to shut up so I could speak, and they did the same thing after I had finished. Some said the Senate never did carry on so over any president or anybody else."
Shut up and sleep with me / Come on, why don't you sleep with me?
He really doesn't know when to shut up and leave it to those at the heart of the negotiations, who fully understand and appreciate all the nuances, to try and hammer out a deal.

glosses: To murder, kill.

examples.text: I just heard that your wife was trying to shut you up for the insurance money.

Shepard: Why were they threatening you? Who do they work for?
Dr. Chloe Michel: They work for Fist. They wanted to shut me up, keep me from telling Garrus about the quarian.

glosses: Closed up or off, as in a building that no one is to enter.

examples.text:
2010. Jem (And Sam). Ferdinand Mount.
She did not come to Court, but she must have been taken to Montagu's house, for the Clerkenwell house was all shut up and was to be sold.

1865. The Wisconsin Farmer, and Northwestern Cultivator, Volume 17. Pg. 75.
Open sheds are too much exposed to drifting snow, and they cannot be shut up and made warm enough for early lambing.

1880. An Earnest Trifler. Mary Aplin Sprague. Pg. 166.
Beaudeck is a very shut-up place.

glosses: Stop talking (usually in the form of making annoying, irrelevant, or false comments, during a period of peace and quiet, or when one is not allowed to talk), arguing, crying, etc.

examples.text: Shut up! We're sick of your whining!

glosses: I don't believe it!, no way!

examples.text: I got accepted to Yale! —Shut up, really? That's awesome!
No, I know what home-school is, I'm not retarded! So you've actually never been to a real school before? Shut up! Shut up!

Jen: Douglas has asked me to be his PA.
Moss: Oh. My. God! Well, that is something and a half. His PA? How... Whoa! His PA... Shut up! His PA!
Jen: It means "personal assistant".
Moss: Thank you. Right, OK. What does that actually involve?

glosses: to stow or secure aloof in a safe place
to obtain passage (on a ship or similar vehicle) by secreting oneself inside before departure

examples.text: Aren't those the things from the station yesterday? They must've stowed away!
